Create a draft contract for a customer's chosen offer.

HTS uses an external payment gateway to tokenize payment cards as well as process payments and payouts.
When HTS is the Merchant of Record (MOR) for the purchase of the order or remitting any product payout to a customer's credit card, HTS requires a tokenized credit card to be present in the `payments` array in the request below.

<details>
<summary>Expand this section for instructions about testing and Spreedly integration.</summary>

The returned payment method token **MxyYEhDK12CUAA18bJDkAq0ab3y** (from the sample response below) should be passed in the `payment_card` type with a `token` identifier as a part of the `payments` array in the request below.

When using the staging environment, make sure to use one of [Adyen's test credit card numbers](https://docs.adyen.com/development-resources/testing/test-card-numbers).

**Tokenization URL**: `https://core.spreedly.com/v1/payment_methods.json`

- Documentation: [Spreedly API docs](https://developer.spreedly.com/reference/create-payment-method)

```

		"email": "aaa@bbb.com",

}'
```

get.description:
Called by HTS to retrieve the current state of a flight booking from the partner system.

HTS provides the booking references stored on the contract as query parameters. These references
are partner-defined key/value pairs (e.g. record locator, order ID) established during contract creation.

The recommended response includes:
- **Booking status** — the current status of the booking (e.g. confirmed, cancelled, voided, pending, checked_in, no_show). Partners may use their own status values; HTS will accept and translate them.
- **Itinerary** — flight slices with segments (origin, destination, departure/arrival times, carrier, flight number, cabin), fare brand, passengers with per-passenger fare amounts, and ancillaries
- **Currency** — ISO 4217 currency code for all monetary amounts
- **Booking references** — the same key/value pairs used to identify the booking
- **Void eligibility** — whether the booking can still be voided (allowed, not_allowed, or allowed_until with an ISO 8601 timestamp)
- **Payment transactions** — amounts, timestamps, transaction types (credit/debit), and payment methods
- **Created at** — ISO 8601 timestamp of when the booking was originally created

Partner implementations may vary in structure and fields returned. HTS is designed to handle
these variations gracefully.

post.description:
Called by HTS to cancel a flight booking in the partner system as part of a contract exercise flow.

HTS provides the booking references in the request body to identify the booking to cancel.

Cancellation may be processed synchronously or asynchronously:
- **202 Accepted** — cancellation initiated asynchronously; HTS will poll or await a callback for completion
- **204 No Content** — cancellation completed synchronously; no response body expected

Partner implementations may vary — some always process cancellations synchronously, others always
asynchronously. HTS is designed to handle these variations gracefully.

Known 422 error codes:
- `already_canceled` — booking has already been canceled
- `last_slice_departed` — booking cannot be canceled because the last slice has already departed

priced.description: Type of offer requested; priced or not. A priced offer can be used to create an order, but has lower rate limits and adds a bit of latency. This should be aligned with the booking flow of the partner: if the offer is made on itineraries that are repriced later in the flow then it’s best to keep it as false here and then call the Price Offers endpoint later in the flow. But if the itinerary is already after the price quote step on the partner side and it might be the final prices we get then setting this option to true returns offers that are priced and can therefore be used as is in the Create Order endpoint, without having to call the Price Offers endpoint. It’s an optimization to facilitate the integration on the partner side. Default: false.

billing_jurisdiction.description: Billing information of the user buying the product(s). Recommended for accurate tax calculations at the price offer step, especially if HTS is merchant of record, to avoid corrections at the create order step since it would be after the user has clicked 'book'. This information is usually not known at this step of the flow, but if the offers are created deep in the funnel it might be available, and if setting priced=true to be able to use the offers in the create order endpoint, then it’s important to use this information here to have accurate pricing. previous_slice_offer_id.description: Used when the partner's booking flow is merchandised one slice at a time. When generating synthetic fares for the first slice, this field should be empty. If the customer has chosen a synthetic fare for the prior slice, the CFAR offer id of the chosen synthetic fare should be stored and passed back into this field when generating synthetic fares for the next slice. The final output will be an offer for the entire itinerary, progressively built from each of the slice selections.

name.description:
The name of the non-refundable discount, e.g. first time booker incentive, etc.
 Set if useful for refund during exercise, e.g. for display, book keeping, etc.

type.description: A discount to the booking that won't be refunded if the booking is canceled or CFAR is exercised. eg: $5 off first time booking.

 Not compatible with HTS as Merchant of Record.

not_provided1.description: Indicates that no email address is available. Only valid when the partner is MOR and cannot provide the email in any form, including hashed. Rejected when HTS is MOR.

not_provided2.title: not_provided
not_provided2.description:
Used when the partner is Merchant of Record and does not provide payment details.
 Payment information is controlled by the partner and not shared with Hopper.

not_provided3.title: not_provided
not_provided3.description:
The partner is Merchant of Record and does not provide payout details to Hopper.
 The partner is responsible for all refund processing.

notification_preferences.title: notification_preferences
notification_preferences.description: Consent for the PRIMARY BOOKER (the email_address / phone_number on this contact_info) to receive disruption notifications via SMS/push. Applies to the primary booker only: additional_recipients never receive SMS or push (they are email-only, notification-only). Captured per offer when the contract is created; does not persist across offers. Recording consent does not trigger delivery.

sms.description: SMS consent for the primary booker's phone_number. Omit = not specified, true = opt-in, false = declined. Requires phone_number to be present; the request is rejected if sms=true and phone_number is absent.

push.description: Push consent for the primary booker. Omit = not specified, true = opt-in, false = declined.

Must include a tokenized payment card if HTS is merchant of record. If both payments and payment_information are provided, payment_information takes precedence.

transaction_type.description: Whether this transaction is a charge or refund.

trip.description: The type of trip the customer is shopping for. This field should only be sent when synthetic fares are being created for partial itineraries which are merchandised slice by slice in the partner's booking flow. Itineraries are assumed by default to be complete, so there is no need to pass the trip type when creating a synthetic fare for the full itinerary.

PartnerAuth.description:
This API supports authentication via API Key. Clients should include their API key in every request using the `X-Api-Key` header.

**Example Request**:

```
curl --request GET --url https://api.hopper.com/v1/example --header 'X-Api-Key: <your-api-key>'
```
PartnerAuth.name: X-Api-Key
